title: Commodity prices broadly unchanged in July — Pink Sheet
gist: The World Bank's July Pink Sheet shows a headline of stability masking violent internal dispersion: the energy index eased 1.1% as coal fell 4.8% and crude 2.2% while European natural gas surged 19.1%, agriculture rose 2.6% purely on a 17.4% beverage jump, and metals fell 2.8% with precious metals down 5.2% led by silver at -11.8%.

themes.theme: Energy: gas dislocation inside a soft index

insights.claim: The World Bank energy price index eased 1.1% in July, driven by coal down 4.8% and crude oil down 2.2%, partly offset by a 19.1% surge in Europe natural gas.
insights.so_what: European gas decoupling violently from coal and crude in the same month points to a region-specific supply or storage shock rather than a global energy demand move.
insights.quote: The energy price index eased 1.1% in July, driven by declines in coal (-4.8%) and crude oil (-2.2%), partly offset by a 19.1% surge in Europe natural gas
insights.locator: The energy price index eased 1.1% in July
insights.speaker: @worldbank

insights.claim: A 19.1% monthly move in European natural gas was large enough to hold a fossil-fuel-heavy index to a mere 1.1% decline despite falls in both coal and crude, showing gas now dominates index volatility.
insights.so_what: For anyone tracking commodity aggregates, headline energy index moves now understate underlying gas risk; trade the components, not the index.
insights.locator: The energy price index eased 1.1% in July
insights.speaker: @worldbank

insights.claim: Agricultural prices rose 2.6% in July even though food prices slipped 0.3% and fertilizer prices dropped 4.3%, with the entire gain driven by a 17.4% jump in beverage prices.
insights.so_what: Soft-commodity strength is narrow and beverage-specific (coffee/cocoa-type exposure), not a broad food inflation impulse — relevant for CPI pass-through assumptions.
insights.quote: Agricultural prices rose 2.6% in July, as a slight decline in food prices (-0.3%) and a 4.3% drop in fertilizer prices were more than offset by a 17.4% jump in beverage prices.
insights.speaker: @worldbank

insights.claim: Fertilizer prices fell 4.3% in July, easing an input cost that feeds directly into next-season planting economics for emerging-market farmers.
insights.so_what: Lower fertilizer costs support margin recovery for agri producers and reduce food-price pressure with a lag of one or more seasons.
insights.speaker: @worldbank

insights.claim: Agricultural raw materials slipped 0.5% in July, a marginal move that contrasts with the sharp beverage move within the same complex.
insights.so_what: Confirms the agriculture gain is not industrial-demand-driven; raw materials, the industrial-linked sub-index, stayed flat to soft.
insights.speaker: @worldbank

themes.theme: Metals and precious metals both down

insights.claim: Metals declined 2.8% in July, led by aluminum down 8.1% with lead and nickel each down 5.3%.
insights.so_what: Broad base-metal weakness with aluminum worst-hit is a negative read on global industrial and construction demand momentum.
insights.quote: Metals declined 2.8% in July, led by aluminum (-8.1%), and lead and nickel (-5.3% each).
insights.speaker: @worldbank

insights.claim: Precious metals fell 5.2% in July, with silver down 11.8% and platinum down 6.0% — a steeper decline than the base-metal complex.
insights.so_what: Precious metals underperforming base metals in a risk-off-looking month is unusual and worth checking against real rates and positioning unwinds.
insights.quote: Precious metals fell 5.2%, reflecting declines in silver (-11.8%) and platinum (-6.0%).
insights.speaker: @worldbank

insights.claim: The non-energy index was broadly unchanged in July, meaning a 2.6% agriculture gain and a 2.8% metals decline effectively cancelled each other out.
insights.so_what: A flat headline hides offsetting sector moves — commodity-linked EM exporters diverged sharply by export basket this month.
insights.quote: The non-energy index was broadly unchanged.
insights.locator: The non-energy index was broadly unchanged
insights.speaker: @worldbank
